title: Lior and the Hymn
premise: Lior Dunmore, a property surveyor, is hired to appraise Hymn House, a derelict estate whose founders built it as an instrument — every room tuned to carry a ritual that was never finished. The house appraises back: it measures Lior's grief, debts, and secrets, and the sleep recordings begin capturing a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud. Drawn into the founders' unfinished rite, Lior discovers the 'justice' the hymn enacts is a devouring of anyone who inherits its power. In the end, Lior completes the ritual deliberately but sings it wrong on purpose, collapsing the hymn into silence and burning the deed — choosing to inherit nothing.
about_author: Odile Dunmore is the pen name of a former land registry clerk who spent a decade cataloguing houses nobody would buy twice. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the terrible patience of buildings.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Grief
chapters.summary: Lior arrives at Hymn House for a routine appraisal, POV theirs throughout. The measurements refuse to reconcile; rooms are larger at night, and the previous surveyor's notes end mid-sentence. Lior keeps the lights on and counts doors obsessively, finding one extra each dusk. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into unease as the house begins taking their inventory in return.

chapters.title: Questions Answered in Sleep
chapters.summary: Lior leaves a recorder running overnight and wakes to a second voice answering questions they never asked aloud — about their mother's will, a debt, a fire. POV alternates between Lior and transcribed recordings. Research reveals the founders' hymn-ritual, designed to judge inheritors. Emotional beat: violation and morbid fascination; Lior realizes the house already knows them intimately.

chapters.title: The Founders' Chorus
chapters.summary: Lior descends into the house's tuned undercroft where the founders' descendants — still living there, unaged — press them toward completing the ritual before the solstice deadline. POV Lior, with the chorus speaking in unison. The hymn begins pulling Lior's memories out as verses. Emotional beat: terror curdling into clarity as Lior sees the 'justice' offered is consumption dressed as judgment.

chapters.title: Sung Wrong on Purpose
chapters.summary: At the solstice climax, Lior takes up the hymn and deliberately corrupts it — flat notes, reversed lines — turning the instrument against its makers. The house devours the chorus instead, then itself. POV Lior, alone in ash and morning light, burning the deed. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won peace; justice achieved outside any law, paid for with everything inherited.
